summary: Design skill for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that builds web pages which avoid the generic look of AI output.
whatItDoes: Hallmark is a design skill you add to a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode. When you ask the agent for a web page, Hallmark picks a visual theme, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and checks the result in a real browser for the habits that make pages look machine-made.
problem: Pages written by AI coding agents often share the same tired patterns, like a small label above every heading or a sign-up box at the end of every page. Hallmark gives the agent rules and checks so the page looks deliberately designed instead.
whoFor: Developers who build websites with AI coding agents
Founders making a landing page or product site
Designers who want an agent to follow firm design rules
Anyone who wants to audit or redesign an existing page
whyChoose: It treats some rules as a hard floor that never ships broken, such as contrast, keyboard focus, reduced motion, a working phone layout and no invented facts, and it has a fresh reviewer look at the page at the end.
requirements: A coding agent: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor or OpenCode
Optional: Chrome and puppeteer-core for the browser checks and screenshots
overview: Hallmark is a skill made by Together AI that changes how your coding agent designs web pages. Instead of the agent's default look, it deals three themes from a catalog of fifty, each one a complete material with its own type, colours, surfaces and components, and lays out the page from the job the page has to do: a booking page books, a shop sells, a newsletter subscribes.

Every build runs through checks in tiers. Floor checks must pass before anything ships, Reflex checks catch the defaults a model tends to fall into, and Finish checks cover craft details without blocking. A lint script renders the page at several widths and a separate reviewer then looks at it with fresh eyes.
You can also point Hallmark at a page you already have: the redesign command keeps your content and wiring while changing the layout and style, and the audit command only reports what it finds.

features.title: Fifty themes
features.body: Each theme is a full material with a sample page, and the build lays out its own page in the chosen one.

features.title: Built from the page's job
features.body: The main action sits where that kind of page normally puts it, and the page ends on it.

features.title: Custom designs
features.body: Ask for custom and Hallmark designs from your prompt alone, under the same rules and checks.

features.title: Uses your real product
features.body: Point it at a URL, a dev server or an app and it captures the screenshots itself.

features.title: Openly licensed photos
features.body: It picks from 755 openly licensed photographs and credits each one it uses on the page.

features.title: Redesign and audit
features.body: Rebuild an existing page while keeping its content and links, or just get a report of the problems.

strengths: Hard rules for contrast, focus, reduced motion and phone layouts
Checks pages in a real browser at several screen widths
Asks for your real photos, screenshots and numbers instead of inventing them
limitations: The browser checks need Chrome and puppeteer-core; without them only the static checks run
Each page is self-contained HTML and CSS, so it may need work to fit into an existing app framework
It runs inside a coding agent, so it uses that agent's model and any costs that come with it

useCases.title: Build a landing page
useCases.body: Describe your product and let the agent build a page in one of the themes.

useCases.title: Restyle an existing site
useCases.body: Run a redesign on your current pages and keep their content and wiring.

useCases.title: Review a page
useCases.body: Run an audit to get a list of the AI-looking habits on a page without changing it.

prerequisites: Optional: Chrome plus puppeteer-core for the render checks

steps.title: Install for every project
steps.body: The -g flag installs it globally. Leave it off to install into the current project only.

steps.title: Or install for one agent only
steps.body: Swap claude-code for codex, opencode, cursor or github-copilot.

steps.title: Optional: enable the browser checks
steps.body: Needed for the rendered lint and screenshots. You also need Chrome installed.

install.label: Install as a Claude Code plugin

steps.title: Install the plugin
steps.body: As a plugin it is invoked as /hallmark:hallmark.

firstRun.title: Ask your agent for a page
firstRun.body: In Claude Code, Cursor or OpenCode, start your request with /hallmark (in Codex use $hallmark), or simply describe a new build. If it doesn't kick in on its own, name it: use hallmark to build a page for my project.

tutorial.title: Audit and redesign an existing page
tutorial.useCase: You already have a site and want to see which parts look AI-generated, then fix them.
setup: Install Hallmark with the skills CLI
Open your coding agent in your project folder

steps.title: Audit the page first
steps.body: This only reports problems and changes nothing.

steps.title: Redesign it
steps.body: Hallmark keeps the content and wiring and changes the layout and style. Say keep the layout for a restyle, or polish for only the small fixes.

steps.title: Lint any page yourself
steps.body: From a clone of the repo, run the lint script on a file or folder.

tutorial.expected: A redesigned page with the same links, fields and headings, plus a side-by-side before and after.
nextSteps: Browse the themes on the Hallmark website
Try a custom design from a prompt

costs.label: Software
costs.value: Free and open source under the MIT licence.

costs.label: AI usage
costs.value: Runs inside your coding agent, so you pay whatever that agent's model usage costs you.

troubleshooting.problem: The skill doesn't run on its own
troubleshooting.solution: Name it in your request, for example: use hallmark to build a pricing page.

troubleshooting.problem: The rendered checks or screenshots don't run
troubleshooting.solution: Install puppeteer-core globally and make sure Chrome is installed; without them only the static checks run.

bestFor: Landing pages built with AI agents
Claude Code, Codex and Cursor users
